newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain truckers join protest, set up barricades.
newsitem.headline: Spain truckers join protest, set up barricades.

text.p: Spanish truckers joined in a European day of action for higher pay and harmonised working conditions by setting up blockades on Monday in three different points at borders with France and Portugal.

"The blockade started this morning at 0600 GMT at la Junquera (A-7) at the border between Catalonia and France, in the Basque Country (close to San Sebastian at N-1) and at Fuentes de Onoro, close to Salamanca at the border with Portugal," said Eladio San Romar, head of the truckers' division of the CCOO union.
He added that the blockade would be lifted at 1100 GMT.
Joining the European protest, Spanish truck drivers intend to ask for an early retirement, at 60 instead of 65, and the recognition of professional sickness, he said.
He added that European legislation permits long work days for truckers. Drivers are particularly upset that they are not paid for time spent while trucks are loaded and unloaded.

A spokesman for the other Spanish union, UGT, said Spain was participating in the European protest because truck drivers were afraid to suffer "from unfair competition due to different legislation in different European member states."
